lit.\u0027Base fuerte pequeña: puede atacar: "Small strong base: it can attack the carbon or remove a β-H; the balance depends on the substrate."
lit.\u0027Base voluminosa: no puede acercars: "Bulky base: it cannot approach the hindered carbon, but it can remove a peripheral H → E2."
lit.\u0027Con un sustrato primario y un reac: "With a primary substrate and a weak reagent the reaction is very slow: a better nucleophile is needed."
lit.\u0027Disolvente aprótico: no solvata an: "Aprotic solvent: it does not solvate anions through hydrogen bonds → more reactive nucleophiles/bases (favors SN2/E2) and it does not stabilize ions (disfavors SN1/E1)."
lit.\u0027Disolvente prótico: estabiliza car: "Protic solvent: it stabilizes carbocations and anions through hydrogen bonds → favors SN1/E1 and tempers anionic nucleophiles."
lit.\u0027El caso secundario con reactivo dé: "The secondary case with a weak reagent usually gives an SN1/E1 mixture (and possible carbocation rearrangements)."
lit.\u0027En un sustrato terciario no hay SN: "With a tertiary substrate there is no SN2; a good, weakly basic nucleophile in a protic medium rather triggers SN1."
lit.\u0027La solvólisis de un halogenuro de: "Solvolysis of a methyl halide is extremely slow: in practice it does not occur without a better nucleophile."
lit.\u0027Nucleófilo fuerte y poco básico: a: "Strong, weakly basic nucleophile: it attacks the carbon rather than removing protons (favors SN2)."
lit.\u0027Reactivo débil: no fuerza reaccion: "Weak reagent: it does not force bimolecular reactions; if anything happens, it goes through a carbocation (SN1/E1) and is slow."
lit.\u0027Sustrato metilo: sin impedimento y: "Methyl substrate: unhindered and with no β carbons → only SN2 is possible."
lit.\u0027Sustrato primario: poco impedido (: "Primary substrate: little hindered (SN2 accessible) and its carbocation would be too unstable (SN1/E1 almost nil)."
lit.\u0027Sustrato secundario: admite SN2 y: "Secondary substrate: allows SN2 and E2; with weak reagents it can ionize slowly (SN1/E1)."
lit.\u0027Sustrato terciario: el impedimento: "Tertiary substrate: steric hindrance blocks SN2, but its carbocation is stable (SN1/E1); with strong bases E2 dominates."
lit.\u0027Temperatura alta: la eliminación g: "High temperature: elimination gains ground (it releases more molecules: entropy increases)."
lit.\u0027Temperatura baja: se favorece la s: "Low temperature: substitution is favored over elimination."
